body:
The scheduled security workflow can be green without either a full dependency-tree audit or a fatal verdict on CodeQL findings. This leaves old pinned vulnerable dependencies and source findings outside the workflow's terminal result.

Reproduction from the current full template tree:

1. Trigger `security.yml` on its weekly schedule. The dependency-review job is PR-only, so it skips; it would only inspect changed dependencies even on a PR. There is no full-tree ecosystem audit in this workflow.
2. Introduce a source issue detected by the selected CodeQL suite. `github/codeql-action/analyze` can successfully produce/upload a SARIF report containing findings while its step succeeds. The separate code-scanning check may report findings, but the workflow/aggregate job observes successful analysis execution.

Concrete downstream evidence: https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/actions/runs/40931698011/job/123652306137 has a successful Analyze step followed by a failing explicit SARIF gate on five findings. The original full SARIF and logs are retained in https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/pull/542 under `dev/log/issues/541/pulls/542/`. That PR also found two previously unaudited pinned fpdf2 advisories using a full Python dependency audit, illustrating the distinction between source scanning, dependency review and full-tree audits.

A small gate regression can use this analysis-success SARIF fixture and must fail on its finding:

```json
{"version":"2.1.0","runs":[{"tool":{"driver":{"name":"CodeQL"}},"invocations":[{"executionSuccessful":true}],"results":[{"ruleId":"example/finding","level":"warning","message":{"text":"reproducing finding"}}]}]}
```

Workaround/suggested implementation: retain SARIF with `analyze`'s output input and add a mandatory validator that rejects every desired finding level, failed tool diagnostic, missing/empty invocation list, unknown execution state, or missing report. For NuGet, run locked restore with `NuGetAuditMode=all` and warnings as errors, then audit all transitive packages and validate its JSON response. For native dependencies, use an ecosystem-supported provider, retain the resolved dependency coordinates, and explicitly report missing provider authorization or unknown packages rather than implying a clean audit. Run the audit on PRs, main and schedules, independently of dependency-review eligibility. Add bounded regressions with a finding and an incomplete scan, and verify that the final workflow gate fails.

Related reports already exist for the other templates: https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/122 and https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/221. This report concerns this template's own security workflow; it does not request copying unrelated language distributions.

## Latest Data.Doublets practices (2026-10-30)

Reviewed downstream main `046c3eaa1de66ff981592bae79365fc2db5397ac` and template main `4cc372ebf2075a0c948b46881143f7d66f0f0e7e`. [Data.Doublets #542](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/pull/542) is merged as `5846b3767e37b711a7119e439275dcb9a848b681`. Its final [run 40937321638](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/actions/runs/40937321638) passed on `f986ec075b692820829dbf57ea278ea598d5f17c`. The later matching-main [run 40970271393](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/actions/runs/40970271393) also succeeded with the security gates and publication. The template still has a PR-only dependency-review job and no explicit full-audit/fatal-SARIF gate; it must not be marked fixed merely because downstream is green.

### Applicable transfer checklist

| Area | Best practice to bring into the C# template | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Explicit CodeQL verdict | Preserve the original SARIF, then fail on every reported finding under the selected policy, including note-level findings if following downstream's strict policy. Fail on absent reports, empty/malformed runs, missing/malformed result lists, missing/unknown/non-successful invocations, and tool warning/error diagnostics. Successful report upload does not mean a clean scan. | [`scripts/check_sarif.py`](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/blob/046c3eaa1de66ff981592bae79365fc2db5397ac/scripts/check_sarif.py) and the original five-finding report in #542 |
| Full dependency graph | Run full direct/transitive NuGet audit on PRs, main and schedules, independently of changed-dependency review. Use locked restore, `NuGetAuditMode=all`, fatal audit warnings/errors and machine-readable audit validation. Distinguish clean, vulnerable and unverified/unreachable-provider outcomes. Save exact resolved package coordinates and report artifacts. | [`scripts/check_audit.py`](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/blob/046c3eaa1de66ff981592bae79365fc2db5397ac/scripts/check_audit.py), audit workflow and #542 |
| All maintained helper code | Keep C# and Actions source analysis. If a generated repository contains maintained Python helpers/experiments, include their CodeQL extraction, pinned lint/format/type checks and full requirements/transitive audit; #542 found two fpdf2 advisories plus five Python CodeQL findings. Adapt equivalent checks to the template's actual JavaScript helpers; do not add unrelated product languages or blindly copy a Python runtime. | #542 and the [complete template comparison](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/blob/5846b3767e37b711a7119e439275dcb9a848b681/dev/log/issues/541/pulls/542/research/TEMPLATE-COMPARISON.md) |
| Workflow and shell lint are real checks | Preserve the template's already digest-pinned complete actionlint image with ShellCheck/Pyflakes. If using a native executable, require those integrations and fail when missing. Extend lint to maintained standalone shell scripts and relevant helper changes, not only workflow-file path filters. Test with a known shell/Python finding; a bare actionlint binary can silently omit integrations. | #542; current template `workflows.yml` already has the full image, so retain that protection |
| Artifact integrity without deprecated extraction | Review each pinned artifact action's actual behavior. Where it still reaches the deprecated `unzip-stream`/Buffer path, use integrity-checked raw downloads and a validated extraction step, or an upstream fixed release proven by a regression. Keep SHA/digest pinning and verification. Reject ambiguous archives, traversal/absolute/drive-qualified paths and symlinks before writing files. Do not solve a warning by suppressing Node deprecations. | [`scripts/extract_artifact.py`](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/blob/046c3eaa1de66ff981592bae79365fc2db5397ac/scripts/extract_artifact.py), [download-artifact #484 evidence](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/issues/484#issuecomment-6505041826) |
| Tests and CI share one policy | Run bounded helper regressions and the same maintained-code lint/type/format policy locally and in CI. Use an always-running terminal required-job gate that rejects failed/cancelled/missing expected work; an intentionally inapplicable job must be distinguished from an incomplete scan. Preserve compiler/analyzer warnings policy and package-consumer checks. | #542 investigation/verification and subsequent successful main run |
| Narrow, evidenced exceptions | Keep immutable research/source snapshots outside maintained-code extraction where justified; scan real helpers/experiments. For a confirmed credential-scanner false positive, scope an exception to the exact historical fingerprint and retain full-history scanning. Do not exclude whole generated/docs trees or globally disable rules to make CI green. | [Data.Doublets #540](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/pull/540) and #542 |
| Native/advisory scope is explicit | Only generated repositories that actually have native dependencies need a provider-specific native audit. Record all resolved coordinates; unavailable provider authorization or unsupported package aliases mean unverified coverage, not zero vulnerabilities. Do not copy the downstream's C++ distribution into this C# template. | #542 retained 19 native coordinates and explicitly reported the provider limitation |

### Acceptance additions

- [ ] A valid SARIF with one finding fails the workflow and required gate; a clean complete report passes. Missing report, empty runs, missing/malformed result lists, absent/empty invocation list, unknown execution status and tool diagnostics fail bounded regressions. An empty result list is valid for a complete clean scan.
- [ ] Full-tree audit detects an existing vulnerable direct **and transitive** package even when no dependency changed. Malformed JSON, network/provider failures, missing graph or skipped expected audit cannot look clean.
- [ ] Required source/helper/security gates run for relevant changes and scheduled/main execution; checks do not disappear behind PR-only eligibility or a workflow-only path filter.
- [ ] Existing complete actionlint integrations remain enabled; native-mode missing-dependency and standalone-shell regressions prove that analysis really happened.
- [ ] A real artifact upload/download round trip passes with deprecations treated as errors, expected bytes/hashes are preserved, and malicious/ambiguous archive fixtures fail before extraction writes.
- [ ] Preserve original SARIF, audit JSON, tested artifact identity and run SHA/URL. Verify the required gate's terminal result, not only individual tool exit codes or uploaded annotations.
- [ ] Keep CodeQL build mode explicit and appropriate for the actual C# project (see #73); do not silently trade away generated-source or build-dependent coverage just to remove an overlay warning.

Release authentication, protected writes, immutable assets and actual public consumers belong to the refreshed #80 checklist. Action pinning/writer queues remain tracked by #72/#79. This update records applicable best practices; it does not close any of these issues or claim that the C# template is already compliant.
title: Scheduled security lacks a full dependency audit and fatal CodeQL findings gate
